subject: project:gdl
value: A splits.txt data-section claim whose END is a round 8-byte boundary while the compiled object's natural section end is 4 bytes short is an OVER-CLAIM that has swallowed LINK-TIME ALIGNMENT PADDING, not evidence of a missing source object. objdiff scores a data section as contributing to matched_data ONLY when it is 100% matched, so a single such 4-byte over-claim zeroes the whole section's contribution: mb_font's .data (0x58 claimed vs 0x54 emitted) and .sdata2 (0x48 vs 0x44) between them cost 152 of 415 data bytes and held the TU at 61.4% data while every byte it emitted was already correct. THREE INDEPENDENT TELLS, all cheap: (1) datadiff.py prints `0xN claim slack(zero)` for exactly this shape - the trailing bytes are present in the DOL and are ZERO; (2) the SAME TU's .rodata claim ends on an odd address (mb_font .rodata 0x80115CE8..0x80115D6F, with mb_lights starting at 0x80115D70) proving the splits author DID exclude inter-TU padding elsewhere, so a neighbouring round-boundary end in the same entry is anomalous; (3) symbols.txt's own size field contradicts its type annotation - `lbl_80348B88 ... size:0x8 align:4 data:float` is self-inconsistent because a float is 4 bytes, and the sibling `lbl_80348B80 ... size:0x8 align:8 data:double` shows the consistent form. DISCRIMINATOR against a genuine missing object: count the relocations. mb_font's .data is entirely a switch jump table; both target and ours carry exactly 21 relocated words (.rela.data 0xFC = 21 Elf32_Rela on BOTH sides), so the target's 22nd word is unrelocated zero and cannot be a table entry - it is padding. A real missing entry would show a relocation count difference. FIX PROCEDURE: shrink the splits.txt end AND the owning symbols.txt size in the same edit - the splitter hard-fails with `Split ... ends within symbol '<name>'` if only splits.txt is changed, which is a useful guard, not an obstacle. The empirical proof that the bytes were link padding is the retail sha1 gate: after shrinking, the linker regenerates the identical DOL because the following TU's section alignment re-creates the pad. NEVER apply this by inference - read the DOL bytes and confirm they are zero first.
